statements.t: We have been negatively impacted and we expect to continue to be negatively impacted by adverse macroeconomic conditions, including tariffs imposed or to be imposed on goods manufactured in Vietnam, Taiwan, the PRC, and Mexico, and reduced consumer spending on durable goods.

Management will continue to seek ways to lessen the impact these pressures may have on our margins and financial results; however, these mitigation efforts may not be successful and these pressures may have a material adverse effect on our business.

In October 2026, the Company’s Board of Directors approved a plan to close the Company’s manufacturing operations in Brazil as part of the Company’s ongoing efforts to optimize its global manufacturing footprint and cost structure.
The Company expects the wind-down of the Brazil operations to be substantially completed during the first quarter of 2027.

The Company currently estimates that it will incur approximately $4.2 million to $5.0 million in costs associated with the closure, primarily consisting of employee severance and other facility closure costs.
Consistent with 2025, we expect the U.S. to be in a pre-tax loss position without benefit for the full year 2026, resulting in an elevated effective tax rate.

We anticipate that we will continue to utilize both cash flows from operations and our revolving lines of credit to support ongoing business operations, capital expenditures, discretionary share repurchases and potential acquisitions.

We believe our current cash balances, anticipated cash flow to be generated from operations and available borrowing resources will be sufficient to cover expected cash outlays for at least the next twelve months and for the foreseeable future thereafter; however, because our cash is located in various jurisdictions throughout the world, we may at times need to increase borrowing from our revolving lines of credit…

In connection with the expected recovery of IEEPA tariffs, the Company evaluated its contractual and customary business practices with customers and concluded that a portion of the expected recovery is likely to be refunded to certain customers.

Accordingly, the Company recorded an estimated liability of approximately $3.9 million as of June 30, 2026 for expected tariff refunds payable to customers, with a corresponding reduction of net sales in the period.
We estimate that we will incur between $1.0 million and $1.5 million during the remainder of 2026.
Additionally, potential future repurchases of shares of our common stock and dividend payments will impact our cash flows used for financing activities.

We anticipate meeting our material cash commitments with our cash generated from operations and available borrowing on our Credit Lines.
• In Q3 2026, we significantly reduced our operational costs, which we believe will improve our ability to generate profits going forward.

We continue to expect adjusted non‑GAAP diluted earnings per share to be in the range of $0.45 to $0.65 for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2026, compared to $0.31 per share in fiscal 2025, consistent with our prior guidance.

We have not provided guidance for GAAP diluted earnings (loss) per share or a reconciliation of forward-looking adjusted non-GAAP diluted earnings per share to the comparable GAAP measure because certain excluded items, including severance, litigation settlements, losses on assets held for sale, foreign currency gains and losses, and related tax effects, cannot be reasonably estimated without unreasonable effort…
